text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a 3x p95 token latency spike on several g4 hosts starting ~09:14 UTC. Correlates with a sharp prefix cache hit-rate collapse across many tenants, acme most visible.

deploy-bot: Deployed commit 4f7a2b to branch/runtime-config at 2026-03-18T09:12:47Z — rollout to g4-fleet

tess: Can you paste the specific cache metrics / p95 numbers?

alex: Sure, pulled from grafana: 
prefix_cache.hit_rate (acme): 0.18 -> 0.02 in ~6m
prefix_cache.global_fill: 92% -> 99%
kv_cache.evictions_per_sec: 1.8k -> 12k
p95_token_latency: 65ms -> 220ms

samir: Did that deploy include any kernel-selection or batching heuristic changes?

mike: Yes — the deploy flipped a canary flag: dynamic_batch_slowdown=true (aim: reduce tail latency under bursty traffic). Also changed prefix_kv_ttl from 30d -> 7d for faster churn testing.

helen: TTL reduction + aggressive batching heuristic could increase item churn and increase prefix key pollution. That explains huge evictions and hit-rate collapse.

tess: Mitigation plan? Roll back TTL and the batching change for canary?

alex: Initiating rollback of TTL on g4-fleet now:
```
configctl set runtime.prefix_kv_ttl=30d --env=g4 --who=alex
```

deploy-bot: Rollback job started (id=rb-20260318-0919).

samir: I'm disabling dynamic_batch_slowdown for the canary group as well.

mike: Also temporarily increasing prefix cache soft-cap for affected shards to avoid immediate evictions. Doing that via runtime override.

alex: After rollback + disable, metrics trending back: prefix_cache.hit_rate -> 0.15 in ~3m, kv_cache.evictions_per_sec down to ~2.1k, p95_token_latency -> ~72ms. Partial recovery.

helen: Root cause summary: inadvertent config change (TTL drop) plus enabling a batching heuristic that increased concurrent prefix churn from a noisy tenant. Eviction storm caused prefix key poisoning across shards and kernel selection regressions due to shifted sequence length distribution.

tess: I'll file a postmortem. Action items: add rollout guardrail for kv_ttl changes, alert on evictions/sec > 5k, add per-tenant cache caps and improved canary controls for batching heuristics, and run an offline replay to validate kernel selection interactions.

mike: Agreed. Also add a quick profiler capture for the runtime when eviction rate spikes so we can see kernel hotpaths and KV lock contention next time.

alex: Thanks folks — keeping an eye on the dashboard, will follow up in the PM with logs and the exact shard ids. :thumbsup:
